verdict: The numbers, the data, the engine change and the saved networks of E3 hold up under independent recomputation; I found no leakage and no arithmetic error. Every headline number of results/more_basins.json (five new sets, seven controls, three leads, and the 20 seed and average files) was reproduced with my own code to 0.0, also by flood.evaluate; the seed averages are bitwise means of their seed files, obs are the project's flow bit for bit, the stored sets hold exactly the 12. The engine change is confined to basins() and load_data(): with no ids the hand-in engine and the present engine rebuild the same 9,543,479-byte cache from the raw files, equal to the stored one; thresholds and the lstm_wq headline (median NSE 0.5896, 18.66% of onsets) are unchanged; no other script passes ids; test_flood.py passes and its new check fails for all eight deliberately broken load_data() variants. The 63 basins are exactly what the audit rule gives (recomputed from the raw files for all 78 candidates), their cache equals tables I rebuilt bit for bit, and the 12 inside it equal the stored 12. All 15 saved networks reproduce their stored forecasts bit for bit from the file alone (also with my own input matrix); their scalers equal my recomputation from the training years of the training rivers; early stopping used the validation years of the 63 (of the 50, never the 12, for the never-seen models). The never-seen training never reads the 12 (fit with the 12 absent from the dictionary gives identical weights); the nested gauge 03471500 lies 100% inside 03473000 and is the only overlapping pair of the 63. The interim scoring pass did not influence the equal-training arm: the 15-training plan is the first line of the log, the killed run printed the arm's curve and the rerun the same numbers, and the other four sets' results are unchanged. The gain rule, its words and all verdicts reproduce exactly. What the experiment shows is smaller than its sentences, and three statements say more than the data. (1) With the gauge, 63 rivers give no clear NSE gain at 1 day (0.590 -> 0.604, inside the 12-river seed range), a clear one at 2 and 3 days (+0.022, +0.028) and much steadier trainings; the onsets are not 'a clear loss': at the fixed level the model warns of 8 fewer onsets and 59 fewer false alarms with the same CSI (McNemar p = 0.24), at the level chosen on validation it warns of more (21.6% against 18.7%); the verdict stays NOT YET (must-fix 1). (2) The 'equal training' arm is not equal at the kept network: its checkpoints are the same early ones as the 1x arm (593 sequences per river against 1689 for the control), because the 63-river validation score peaks at 1000-1500 updates; it shows that a longer patience window does not move the optimum. (3) For rivers never seen, 50 training rivers give +0.16 (with properties) and +0.12 (weather only) NSE over the 05 numbers in every seed, and that survives the seed-average and budget differences; but it compares a three-seed average of one model with single trainings (a single seed's p is 0.05-0.09 with properties), and it cannot be attributed to the number of rivers: it does not rank with the distance to the nearest training gauge (rho -0.36, p 0.26) and the 50-river networks do not score lower on 27 never-seen rivers the farther they lie (rho +0.09), yet the two designs differ in number, variety and neighbours at once; the test that would separate scale from proximity (buffered leave-out, dose-response) needs training and was not done. Open before E3 can enter the report: must-fix 1 and 2 and the wording items of should-fix 1 to 5; the outcome sentence is fair arithmetic but must not be quoted without a corrected outcome_caveat.
